transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

I'm here because... well, for almost two years now, I've just been unable to shake this certainty that a few people in the ensemble I direct are quietly trying to undermine my work. It started right after a commission I did. They do it through these subtle things—using schedule changes, seating choices, little comments during rehearsals. And, I mean, even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away... I just know what they're actually doing. It's been going on for a long time, and I guess I just needed to talk to someone about it.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people could not?
No, nothing like that. I've never heard voices or... seen things that aren't there. Everything I'm talking about is just happening in real life, right in front of me during rehearsals.
When other people give you clear evidence that these ensemble members are not trying to undermine you, are you able to consider that you might be mistaken?

Honestly, no. I really can't. Like I mentioned a minute ago, even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, I just can't shake the certainty that they're doing it. It's been almost two years since that commission, and I see exactly how they use those schedule changes, the seating choices, the little comments in rehearsals... I just know they are quietly undermining my work. So when people try to give me evidence to the contrary, it doesn't change my mind, because I know what's actually happening.
Aside from this belief about your ensemble, have you noticed yourself becoming much less able to work or manage daily life than before?

No, I haven't. Outside of this whole issue with the ensemble, everything else is actually fine. I still meet all my deadlines, and I keep up with my composing without any problems. I even go for a run most mornings. And things at home with my wife are basically steady. So, no, it hasn't stopped me from managing my daily life... it's really just this one specific situation at work that's so frustrating.
Do you believe these ensemble members have any unusual power or method to influence events around you in a way other people normally could not?

No, I don't think they have any sort of... supernatural powers or anything like that. They're just regular people. They just use normal, everyday things to mess with my work—like I said, the schedules, the seating, the side conversations. It's not magic, it's just... it's just very coordinated and intentional. But no, they don't have any unusual methods or anything impossible. They're just musicians being petty and vindictive.
Before this started two years ago, did you generally tend to mistrust other people’s motives?

No, not really. Before all this started, I was pretty trusting, I think. I mean, I never really had a reason not to be. I got along well with people in grad school and in other groups I worked with. I didn't walk around thinking people were out to get me or anything. It's just... this specific group, with this specific commission. That's when things changed, because of what they started doing. But before that, no, I didn't have any issues trusting people's motives.
Has anyone told you that your speech or behavior has become noticeably disorganized or hard to follow?

No, nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I think I communicate pretty clearly, actually. I mean, my wife hasn't mentioned anything, and I have to be really organized and clear when I'm composing or talking to other musicians. So, no, my speech and behavior are completely normal.
During this period, have you had a time when you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric for days at a time?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I mean, I get focused when I'm working on a piece, sure, but not... not unusually high or euphoric. Just normal energy levels, really. Nothing out of the ordinary.
When this first began, did the experience come on very suddenly over a few days?

No, it wasn't sudden like that. It didn't just happen over a few days. It was more of a gradual thing, I guess. I just started putting the pieces together over time, noticing the little things they were doing with the commission. So, no, it wasn't an overnight realization or anything sudden.
